The '''2026 United States Senate election in''' '''Oregon''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Oregon]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Jeff Merkley]] is seeking a fourth term.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.opb.org/article/2025/07/10/jeff-merkley-seeking-4th-term/|title=Oregon’s Jeff Merkley will seek a 4th term in US Senate, ending speculation|last=VanderHart|first=Dirk|publisher=[[Oregon Public Broadcasting]]|access-date=July 11, 2025|date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state senator [[David Brock Smith]].<ref name="Smith Wins">{{cite web|last=Rush|first=Claire|date=May 22, 2026|title=David Brock Smith wins GOP primary for US Senate in Oregon, will face Democratic incumbent Merkley|url=https://apnews.com/article/oregon-primary-election-2026-republican-senate-32d9f95d985f971380476246c6f6b723|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260523193932/https://apnews.com/article/oregon-primary-election-2026-republican-senate-32d9f95d985f971380476246c6f6b723|archive-date=May 23, 2026|url-status=live|access-date=May 23, 2026|work=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

In the Democratic primary, Merkley was nominated with 93.2% of the vote against minimal opposition. Smith won the Republican nomination with 29.5% of the vote over former Linn County party chair [[Jo Rae Perkins]] and real estate broker Brent Barker.

Republicans have not won a Senate election in Oregon since [[2002 United States Senate election in Oregon|2002]].
